subtitle: Seven Centuries Around a Single Lake

panels.shot: sweeping high-angle wide over Sudarshana Lake with Girnar hills behind and Suvishakha in the foreground
panels.action: Suvishakha, son of Kulaipa, stands on the stone embankment of Sudarshana Lake as storm clouds and sun share the sky, the Girnar hills looming behind and ancient masonry stretching away under his feet.

dialogue.text: At Girnar, one lake outlived Mauryas, Yavanas, Sakas and Guptas, and in its cracked stones Suvishakha, son of Kulaipa, read a seven-hundred-year duty no flood could wash away.

i18n.hi: गिरनार पर एक झील ने मौर्य, यवन, शक और गुप्तों को झेला, और उसकी दरकी सिलाओं में कुलैपपुत्र सुविशाख ने सात सौ साल का वो धर्म पढ़ा जिसे कोई बाढ़ न बहा सकी।

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye of arid Saurashtra landscape with a new reservoir gleaming
panels.action: A broad view of a dry Saurashtra plain in the age of Chandragupta Maurya, fields and sparse trees stretching out, with a freshly constructed reservoir catching the light at the foot of the Girnar hills.

dialogue.text: Long before Rudradaman, under Chandragupta Maurya, his governor Pushyagupta dammed the streams of Girnar to form Sudarshana, a shining lake in a thirsty land.

i18n.hi: रुद्रदामन से बहुत पहले, चन्द्रगुप्त मौर्य के समय, उनके सूबेदार पुष्यगुप्त ने गिरनार की धाराएँ बाँधकर सूदर्शन बनाया — प्यासे देस में चमकती झील।

panels.shot: medium wide on the dam with water channels extending, early morning light
panels.action: Masons and workers in Mauryan dress lay massive stone blocks across a valley while channels branch away, the new embankment holding back a swelling sheet of water that reflects the pale dawn.

dialogue.text: The inscription remembers his work: Sudarshana’s embankment, the stone raised, the waters gathered, so that fields might drink and caravans might halt by a cool shore.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख उसके काम को याद रखता है: सूदर्शन का बाँध, उठी हुई चट्टानें, रोकी गई धाराएँ, ताकि खेतों को घूँट मिले और क़ाफिले ठंडी तट पर दम ले सकें।

panels.shot: low-angle on a Greek-looking official overseeing channels carved in stone
panels.action: A Yavana official in simple robes, Tushaspha, stands by the dam as workers cut new stone channels into the bank, water beginning to flow in clear streams under his watchful gaze.

dialogue.text: Under Ashoka, a Yavana named Tushaspha added conduits, guiding the lake’s waters with care, proof that men from far coasts now shared in the emperor’s charge.

i18n.hi: अशोक के अधीन, तुषास्फ़ नाम के यवन ने नालियाँ जोड़ीं, झील का पानी सँभालकर मोड़ा — सबूत कि दूर तटों के लोग भी अब सम्राट का भार बाँट रहे थे।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide, same lake across changing ages, fading empires in background
panels.action: The scene shows the same lake under different rulers suggested in the distance: Mauryan banners fading, new banners of later dynasties rising, while the embankment and waters endure in the foreground.

dialogue.text: Empires rose, edicts faded, new powers stamped coins in Saurashtra, yet Sudarshana held, a quiet witness, feeding villages that forgot who first ordered its stones.

i18n.hi: साम्राज्य उठे, फरमान घिसे, सौराष्ट्र में नई मुहरें चमकीं, पर सूदर्शन टिका रहा — खामोश गवाह, उन गाँवों को सींचता जो भूल चुके थे किसने पहली बार पत्थर लगवाए।

panels.shot: medium close on Suvishakha reading an inscription on rock, light slanting across the script
panels.action: Suvishakha, in the dress of a Pahlava minister, runs his fingers over old letters carved on the rock near the lake, his face intent as sunlight grazes the weathered script.

dialogue.text: Then came the Saka year seventy-two. Under Rudradaman, his minister Suvishakha, son of Kulaipa, looked upon this old work and upon words cut into stone before his time.

i18n.hi: फिर आया शक संवत बहत्तर। रुद्रदामन के समय, उनका मंत्री कुलैपपुत्र सुविशाख इस पुरानी रचना को देखने आया, और अपने से पहले की नक़्क़ाशी हुई पंक्तियों को भी।

panels.shot: wide shot of the lake and embankment under darkening storm clouds, Suvishakha tiny in foreground
panels.action: From a distance, Suvishakha stands as a small figure on the embankment while heavy monsoon clouds gather over the Girnar hills, the wind already churning the lake’s surface into restless waves.

dialogue.text: The record speaks of a violent storm. Clouds broke, winds struck, and the proud embankment faced a test harsher than any king’s decree.

i18n.hi: ब्योरा एक प्रचंड आँधी का है। बादल फटे, आँधियाँ चलीं, और गर्वीला बाँध किसी भी राजा के हुक्म से कठोर कसौटी पर आ टकराया।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of water crashing against the dam at night
panels.action: Under a black sky split by lightning, surging water hammers against the stone embankment, spray leaping into the air as parts of the structure strain and begin to give way.

dialogue.text: Rain poured, streams swelled, and Sudarshana’s calm mirror became a force. Somewhere in that dark, stones shifted and the barrier that held back life began to break.

i18n.hi: मूसलाधार बरसा, धाराएँ फूल उठीं, और सूदर्शन का सुकूनभरा दर्पण ताक़त बन गया। अँधेरे में कहीं पत्थर सरके, और जो बाँध जीवन थामे था, वही टूटने लगा।

panels.shot: morning-after wide of a breached embankment with people watching in shock
panels.action: In the grey light after the storm, villagers and officials stand on the shore staring at a great gap in the embankment where water still rushes out, the lake level visibly fallen and fields below soaked and ruined.

dialogue.text: By morning, the breach gaped wide. The inscription measures it in hands and cubits; the lake’s wealth now spilled uncontrolled, a blessing turned sudden peril.

i18n.hi: सुबह तक दरार मुँह बाये खड़ी थी। शिलालेख उसे हथेलियों और हाथों में नापता है; झील की दौलत अब बेकाबू बह रही थी — नेमत जो पल में आफ़त बनी।

panels.shot: medium on Suvishakha kneeling at the broken edge, examining with focused calm
panels.action: Suvishakha kneels at the jagged end of the shattered embankment, hands on the exposed stones and earth, his expression steady as he studies the damage rather than the watching crowd.

dialogue.text: Suvishakha did not stand apart. The rock record calls him Pahlava minister, yet here he is in the broken mud, reading the breach as a scribe reads a line gone wrong.

i18n.hi: सुविशाख अलग नहीं खड़ा रहा। शिला उसे पहलव मंत्री कहती है, पर यहाँ वो कीचड़ में उतरता है, टूटन को वैसे पढ़ता जैसे लिपिक बिगड़ी पंक्ति पढ़े।

panels.shot: intimate close-up on Suvishakha’s face as he thinks, villagers blurred behind
panels.action: A close view of Suvishakha’s weathered, thoughtful face as he looks past the breach to the distant fields, villagers in simple clothes faintly visible behind him, anxious and expectant.

dialogue.speaker: suvishakha_son_of_kulaipa
dialogue.text: If this lake fails, it is not stone alone that breaks.

i18n.hi: अगर ये झील टूटेगी, तो सिर्फ़ पत्थर नहीं टूटेंगे।

panels.shot: courtly interior medium shot with Suvishakha addressing unseen Rudradaman
panels.action: Inside a modest hall, Suvishakha stands respectfully before an unseen throne, his right hand raised in explanation, a tablet or palm-leaf in his left, suggesting he presents a plan rather than a plea.

dialogue.text: The inscription praises Rudradaman, but it is Suvishakha who is named as doer. He sought permission not to tax, not to conscript, but to repair what earlier kings had entrusted.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख रुद्रदामन की प्रशंसा करता है, मगर कर्ता के रूप में नाम सुविशाख का है। उसने इजाज़त माँगी, न करवसूल के लिए, न फौज खड़ी करने को, बल्कि उन कामों को सँवारने को जो पहले के राजाओं ने सौंपे थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of organized workers at the dam, clearly free labourers with tools
panels.action: Lines of workers, artisans and villagers move stones and earth in an orderly fashion along the embankment, some laughing, some focused, with Suvishakha standing among them giving calm instructions, no guards driving them.

dialogue.text: Rudradaman’s rock-edged words boast: the work was done without levying new taxes, without using forced labour. Suvishakha had to rebuild with the means already in his hands.

i18n.hi: रुद्रदामन की शिला‑कटी पंक्तियाँ शान से कहती हैं: ये काम बिना नया कर लगाए, बिना बेगार के हुआ। सुविशाख को वही साधन जुटाने पड़े जो पहले से उसके हाथ में थे।

panels.shot: low-angle on Suvishakha guiding placement of a huge stone block
panels.action: From a low angle, Suvishakha signals with both hands as a team eases a massive stone block into place at the breach, ropes taut and muscles straining, the new stone aligning with the old embankment.

dialogue.text: Block by block, he closed the measured gap. The verse lists lengths and heights, as if to say: this is not a vague promise, but a wall of exact stone and span.

i18n.hi: वो दरार उसने गिन‑गिन कर पत्थर से भरी। श्लोक में लंबाई‑ऊँचाइयाँ दर्ज हैं, मानो कह रहा हो: ये कोई हवा‑हवाई वादा नहीं, बल्कि नपातुल दीवार है, ठोस पत्थर और बाँह की चौड़ाई की।

panels.shot: medium shot of Suvishakha inspecting a newly shaped spillway, water flowing gently
panels.action: Suvishakha stands beside a carefully shaped outlet where water now spills in a controlled sheet into a channel below, his hand testing the flow as craftsmen watch for his nod.

dialogue.text: He restored not only height but outlets, so that the next storm’s fury might find a guided path, and the lake could hold strong without drowning the land it served.

i18n.hi: उसने केवल ऊँचाई नहीं, निकास भी लौटाए, ताकि अगली आँधी की जिद तय राह पाए, और झील ज़मीन को डुबोए बिना मज़बूत रहे।

panels.shot: wide pastoral shot of full lake, irrigated fields and villagers at ease
panels.action: Sudarshana Lake now lies full and calm under a clear sky, its embankment neat and solid; below, green fields stretch out, farmers tending crops and children playing along the water’s edge.

dialogue.text: When the waters settled again behind their stone, life resumed its quieter rhythm. The same lake that once threatened now fed, the danger turned back into daily grain.

i18n.hi: जब पानी फिर पत्थर के पीछे थिर हो गया, जीवन अपनी धीमी चाल पर लौट आया। वही झील जो कल खतरा थी, आज फिर खुराक बनी — ख़तरा लौटकर रोज़ की रोटी हो गया।

panels.shot: close shot of the Junagadh rock inscription being carved
panels.action: A stonecutter carefully chisels Sanskrit letters into the rock face near the lake, another man reading from a palm-leaf beside him, the freshly carved lines crisp against the ancient stone.

dialogue.text: To fix this work in memory, Rudradaman’s men carved the tale on the very rock of Girnar, naming Pushyagupta, Tushaspha and Suvishakha in one flowing line of time.

i18n.hi: इस काम को याद में बाँधने को, रुद्रदामन के लोगों ने यही कथा गिरनार की चट्टान पर काटी, एक ही बहती पंक्ति में पुष्यगुप्त, तुषास्फ़ और सुविशाख का नाम जोड़ते हुए।

panels.shot: time-shift wide showing the same rock centuries later with Skandagupta’s inscription added
panels.action: The same rock appears centuries later, weathered and cracked, with fresh lines of script being cut lower down as another artisan works, while the outline of Sudarshana Lake glimmers in the distance.

dialogue.text: Yet the lake was not finished with storms. Long after Rudradaman, Skandagupta recorded another repair, another ruler answering the same call from the same worn stones.

i18n.hi: पर झील का हिसाब आँधियों से खत्म नहीं हुआ। रुद्रदामन के बहुत बाद, स्कन्दगुप्त ने एक और मरम्मत दर्ज की — वही पत्थर, वही पुकार, उसे फिर एक नए शासक ने सुना।

panels.shot: concluding medium-wide of Suvishakha’s figure silhouetted against the lake and hills at sunset
panels.action: At sunset, Suvishakha stands in silhouette atop the embankment, the calm lake and distant Girnar hills glowing red and gold behind him, his posture quiet, almost merging with the line of stone he restored.

dialogue.text: Sudarshana’s story shows how public works can outlast dynasties, and how a minister like Suvishakha, son of Kulaipa, makes duty to the living as enduring as any conquest cut in stone.

i18n.hi: सूदर्शन की कहानी दिखाती है कि लोककार्य वंशों से लंबा जीते हैं, और कुलैपपुत्र सुविशाख जैसे मंत्री के लिए जीवितों का धर्म उतना ही टिकाऊ हो सकता है जितनी पत्थर में कटी कोई विजय।

title_i18n.hi: झील जो साम्राज्यों के पार फिर से बनी

subtitle_i18n.en: Seven Centuries Around a Single Lake
subtitle_i18n.hi: सात सदियाँ, एक ही झील के इर्द‑गिर्द
